file.

    go build -o kosika-native.exe .

23:conformance/README.md:7208:Today there are two engines: the reference engine in `kosika/` (Python)
and the native engine in `native/` (Go). The native engine exists so that
Kosika can run on a machine with no Python.

## What is here

24:conformance/README.md:25321:
For each `.kos` file, `ENGINE test FILE` must print exactly the text in
the file beside it, and end with exit code 0 when every test passed, 1
when one failed, and 2 when the program was refused before it ran. A
refused program prints `Check failed: ` and the reason, and nothing else. Line ends may be `\n` or `\r\n`.

18:native/README.md:7361:    kosika-native test FILE.kos      run the tests the file carries
    kosika-native tokens FILE.kos    the file's tokens, one JSON object a line
    kosika-native run FILE.kos --input IN.json --model qwen2.5:7b
                                     run a workflow, asking a real model
    kosika-native replay TRACE.jsonl check a run's trace, running nothing

19:native/README.md:31349:and prints the action to approve, and `--approval-record FILE` (or
`--approve`, asking at the terminal) lets it run, once. Begun again, a run
takes what it already did from its journal and does nothing twice. The
journal is this engine's own: two JSON files, not the reference's SQLite,
so an approval given to one engine does not serve the other.

19:native/README.md:43329:lists, maps and optional values. Whole numbers are exact at any size.

Models, with the records they take and give, and general ones that take
and give text. Workflows, whose steps call
a function, run another workflow, use a tool through an agent, or ask a
model (asked again on a refused answer with `retry`), ask an agent, or
19:native/README.md:55309:agent's tools, each answer given back to it, until it answers. A tool that
changes the world is refused, as the reference refuses it without a
recorded approval.

Before it runs a program it checks it, as the reference does: a program
whose types do not agree is refused, with the reference's own message, on
19:native/README.md:61345:the output and with exit code 2. A name the file uses but never declares is
refused as the file is read, like a fault in the text.

Memories and boards, as the reference has them: each is made two tools
that only look, used through a generated agent. `run --memory FOLDER`
keeps a program's memories there, one JSON file a memory written as the
19:native/README.md:73246:refused beside it, and a broken file is refused with the reference's
words and place.

It is held to the conformance suite in `../conformance`, where it must
print what the reference engine prints, word for word. See
`tests/test_conformance.py`.
23:conformance/README.md:1212:# Kosika conformance suite

What Kosika means, written as programs with the results they must give.
An engine is an implementation of Kosika if it passes this suite. The
suite, not any one engine, is the judge.

## What it does not have yet

- Models that answer `as text`, and steps with `verify`, `vote`,
  `escalate`, `learn` or `with evidence`, and
  `parallel` blocks.

- An agent's plan that writes files, or an agent with its own `check`:
  the reference checks such a plan before showing it, and those checks are
  not here yet, so such a plan is refused by name. Replaying an agent
  run's own trace, an answer with evidence, or a verified answer.
- `system` tools other than files and shell (web, kosika, meaning, agents,
  outside), and `fetch`; so an environment's `allow site` grants nothing
